explanation: One of the twelve tribes of Israel, founded by Jacob's firstborn son.
Another of the twelve tribes of Israel, founded by Jacob's seventh son.
The area assigned to a tribe, in this case east of the Jordan River.
A river in the Middle East that serves as a border between the lands of Canaan and Moab.
An ancient kingdom east of the Dead Sea and the Jordan River, often in conflict with Israel.
The prophet and leader of the Israelites who led them out of Egypt and through the wilderness toward Canaan.
Soldiers from the tribes of Reuben and Gad who fought in the war against Midian and other enemies.
Land and possessions given to descendants or tribes as part of God's promise.
A commitment or guarantee given by God to the Israelites to give them a specific territory.
